verdicts.note: archive.org OCR full text of wdh, credits block under the WATERDEEP DRAGON HEIST title; OCR renders it with doubled spaces ('Managing  Editor:  Jeremy  Crawford'), otherwise word for word. Same credits block also lists Crawford under Rules Development, and Christopher Perkins as Lead Designer and Lead Editor. Fetched raw with a browser UA; text read directly from the page's <pre> block, not a summary.

verdicts.trueWording: distributed by Wizards of the Coast to official play writers
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture 20240423102657id_ of dmsguild.com/product/267467. Product description sentence begins 'These PDF documents are distributed by Wizards of the Coast to official play writers and are now available for all DMsGuild creators.' Both limbs (PDF documents; official play writers) present.

verdicts.trueWording: The House Style Guide has been updated January 2019.
verdicts.note: Same Wayback capture; the line sits at the head of the description prefixed 'Note:'. Page's own File Last Updated field reads February 22, 2019, which does not contradict the January 2019 update note for the House Style Guide component.

verdicts.trueWording: tips for adventure design from Chris Perkins and Greg
verdicts.note: Same Wayback capture: 'In addition to the D&D House Style Guide, this package includes tips for adventure design from Chris Perkins and Greg Bilsand...'. The quoted fragment is word for word. FLAG: the page misspells the surname as 'Bilsand'; the string 'Bilsland' does not occur on this page, though the guide PDF itself is bylined 'Greg Bilsland'. The claim's spelling is correct for the person, not for this page.

verdicts.trueWording: Following these style guides is not required to publish on
verdicts.note: Same Wayback capture; the sentence continues 'DMsGuild, but they are provided here at the request of our community creators.' 'the platform' in the claim is DMsGuild, named on the page.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'distributed with the house style guide' - the PDF says nothing about its distribution or about the House Style Guide package; that limb rests on the separate DMs Guild product page (index 1135), not on this page
verdicts.note: PDF fetched (HTTP 200, 2 pages, 745,871 bytes) and text extracted with pdftotext -layout. The title line reads 'WRITING ADVENTURES  By Chris Perkins & Greg Bilsland' - byline verbatim. The document self-titles 'WRITING ADVENTURES'; 'adventure design guide' is the filename and the DMs Guild description's wording. Host is a third-party WordPress reupload, so the copy is a mirror, not a Wizards-hosted original.

verdicts.trueWording: present information as concisely as possible, to ease the burden
verdicts.note: General Principles item 7 opens 'An adventure should strive to present information as concisely as possible, to ease the burden on the DM.' Quote verbatim; the DM limb is on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: namely NPCs, dungeon dressings, and treasure hoards
verdicts.note: Item 7 continues 'However, there are certain elements of an adventure that deserve special attention, namely NPCs, dungeon dressings, and treasure hoards.' The page's own words are 'deserve special attention'; the descriptive-text limb is then made explicit in the same item - NPCs get described features and a striking dungeon feature or treasure 'can also benefit from a splash of descriptive text'. 'Despite the concision rule' is carried by the item's 'However'.

verdicts.trueWording: distinctive physical features, mannerisms, and quirks
verdicts.note: Item 7: 'You can add character to any NPC by describing his or her distinctive physical features, mannerisms, and quirks (which the DM can then use to roleplay the NPC effectively).' Every limb present.

verdicts.trueWording: The goal isn't to keep the DM in suspense
verdicts.note: General Principles item 6, with the curly apostrophe as quoted. Same item carries the second limb: 'the adventure shouldn't conceal or bury important information that the DM needs to understand what's really going on.'

verdicts.trueWording: make sure that an NPC is properly introduced before casually
verdicts.note: Item 6 continues '...mentioning the NPC by name in running text', which is the claim's 'by name in passing'. The rule is framed as an example of presenting information in a logical order.

verdicts.trueWording: An adventure is about the here and now.
verdicts.note: General Principles item 4; the next sentence supplies the history limb - a little history may set things up, 'but the less of it, the better.'

verdicts.trueWording: The Chicago Manual of Style (16th edition) and the
verdicts.note: Closing line: 'For rules on grammar and punctuation, please see The Chicago Manual of Style (16th edition) and the D&D House Style Guide. For adventure format, refer to the Adventure Format Template.' All three limbs (grammar/punctuation, CMoS 16th, House Style Guide) present.

verdicts.trueWording: communicating the basic info and less on dazzling the audience
verdicts.note: mimir.net fetched live, HTTP 200; page title 'An Interview with Ray and Val Vallese - Planescape: I am the Mimir', Gen Con '99 framing. The passage answers the question 'Ray, how did writing this book differ from others, such as PS supplements, you've written?', so the speaker is Ray Vallese. Page reads 'focus more on communicating the basic info and less on dazzling the audience with clever prose' - the claim's 'rather than' compresses the more/less construction; 'basic information' is 'basic info' on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: purchased PS products just to read them
verdicts.note: Same Ray Vallese answer, parenthetical immediately after the supplements rule: 'Granted, that's not entirely true for the PS line, as many people have remarked that they've purchased PS products just to read them.' Qualification, Planescape line and the many-people-remarked limbs all present; 'bought' = 'purchased'.
